_about: QA scenario suite for the items API (NT-3, verifies merged NT-2). Pure JSON/HTTP — no browser DOM. Every scenario drives the real API with `api` steps and asserts the outcome with `capture_equals` (owned-data by form, per SUITES.md §8), namespacing created rows with {{run_id}}. The CRUD round-trip proves the backend effect by deleting the row and re-GETting it for a 404. The `_about`/`_note` fields are documentation only and ignored by the loader.

scenarios.name: Health check responds 200 at the unprefixed root

steps._note: GET /health is unversioned and unprefixed; status:200 pins the code (a non-200 gates the step).

scenarios.name: Items CRUD round-trip: create, read, list, update, delete, then 404

steps._note: Create a namespaced item. status:201 asserts the created code; capturing all four fields asserts the response carries the { id, name, description, createdAt } shape (a missing field fails the capture).
OUTCOME — the create response echoed the name we sent (owned-data: the value was produced by this run).
steps.intent: create response echoes our namespaced name

steps._note: OUTCOME — the create response echoed the description we sent.
Read the item back by id; capture the name for assertion.
OUTCOME — the fetched item has the name we created (proves the row persisted).
steps.intent: GET by id returns our namespaced name

steps._note: List all items; capture the whole array to prove our row is present in the collection view.
Count only OUR row in the list by matching the captured id — owned-data by form (peers carry a different id). Minimal JSONPath can't count, so jq does it.
steps.intent: count our item in the list by id

steps._note: OUTCOME — exactly one of our rows appears in GET /v1/items.
steps.intent: our item appears exactly once in the list

steps._note: Update the description; status:200 pins the PATCH code, capture the returned description.
OUTCOME — the PATCH response carries the new description.
steps.intent: PATCH response returns the new description

steps._note: BACKEND EFFECT — re-GET and confirm the update persisted, not just echoed.
OUTCOME — the persisted description matches what we PATCHed.
Delete our item; status:204 pins the No Content code (also our namespaced-data cleanup).
BACKEND EFFECT — the deleted id now 404s, proving DELETE removed the row (not just returned 204). status:404 makes not-found the expected outcome.

scenarios.name: Validation: create rejects empty and missing name with 400

steps._note: Empty name is invalid; status:400 pins the rejection and bypasses the non-2xx guard so this is the expected outcome.
steps.intent: POST /v1/items with empty name is rejected 400

steps._note: Missing name entirely is also invalid -> 400.
steps.intent: POST /v1/items with missing name is rejected 400

scenarios.name: Versioning: the unversioned items path is not served

steps._note: GET /items (no /v1) must 404 — the API is only exposed under the version prefix.
